_about: Settings for src/score_agents.py. Weights say how much each part counts in the coaching index; they are rescaled to add to 1 for agents missing a part. A part with weight 0 is still shown, but as context only, with no 'clearly above/below' call.
_weights_note: Phase 5: still seller only. Buyer score: needs an independent value estimate of the home (about 4% typical miss or better, made before and without the sale price); a 1-5 condition rating, even a perfect one, barely helps (src/condition_test.py). Offer score: since Phase 5 this is the fair offer score (same home, same price and terms), not the raw win rate. It ranks agents well (0.89) and 98% of its clear calls are right, but it missed the rule set before testing: its 95% ranges catch the truth 87-88% of the time (rule: 90%) and it leans slightly toward agents whose clients pay less (0.16 in one kind of world, rule: 0.15). Next test: widen its ranges using these worlds, confirm on new ones (src/offer_validate.py). Phase 3 weights were seller 0.5, buyer 0.3, offer_win 0.2. Turn a part back on only after validation shows it works on the data you have.
_range_options: Which 95% range decides 'clearly above/below average': formula (2C), bootstrap (3-3), or wider (whichever is wider, so we never overclaim).
_bias_allowance: Extra room for bias the ranges can't see (hidden home quality). 0.008 means we assume up to about 0.8 percentage points of bias (one standard deviation), so seller and buyer ranges are always at least about 1.6 points either side. Sized on fake data so agents with 50+ deals are caught about 95% of the time. On real data this is an assumption, not a measurement.
